Messages.Author: J Greely
Messages.Body:
In article <338qc6$pie@vixen.cso.uiuc.edu> lartigue@prairienet.org
 (Dave A. Lartigue) writes:
>So, just to be the first to start polling, what do YOU use for your EDGE 
>counter in Jyhad?

While I was in the glass store buying red "globs" (blood counters at a
much better price), I picked up a few larger ones, including one large
faceted red teardrop.  At Origins they were using little ankhs
(presumably Vampire: The Masquerade paraphenalia).  In our first game,
we used a handy D20, since no one had brought anything else.

  Another item I have handy is a small disposable razor blade in a red
plastic holder (an Olfa Touch-Knife, for those who hit the art
stores), with a very nice "edge".  It would probably not be a good
idea to use an ornate fantasy dagger or unloaded handgun, though, just
in case a rules discussion got out of hand...

  So how about alternate suggestions for blood counters, too?  We
shouldn't *all* play with boring red globs.  I suggest dropping by
your local gun shop and picking up some clean, unprimed brass in your
favorite caliber, giving it a thin gloss lacquer coat to keep it from
tarnishing, and using a dummy round in a rifle caliber for the Edge.
No live ammo, please.

  Those who don't want to spend money on glass counters can easily
acquire flat plastic counters in any number of colors, or go with
poker chips (too big, imho).  Computer nerds may opt for thin-net
terminators.  When in doubt, there's always pennies; they have the
virtue of being both cheap and available in unlimited quantities.  If
you insist your counters must be red, buy a small can of spray-paint,
and make those pennies bleed.  The obvious choice for the Edge is a
quarter.
--
J Greely (jgreely@synopsys.com)

Edge Counter:

Real Men use a very sharp, long sword that they call a knife.
Real Roleplayers use a wine glass with Black Cherry Kool-aid.

Munchkins use the counters from the blood bank and slip themselves
